name: Arms Control Association (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: a nuclear war kills people everywhere and the future lost is everyone's, so the result is spread by world population.
summary: The Arms Control Association (Washington DC) works to cut the risk of nuclear war through policy research and issue briefs, the journal Arms Control Today, media and congressional engagement and convenings of the field's campaigners; this model covers all its programmes in the year to June 2025 ($1.7M spent). At the defaults it averts about 41 years of healthy life per $1,000, from 1.9 to 900 on the combined range: each dollar is valued as a typical project's cut in the forecast risk of nuclear war (Rethink Priorities' cross-cause model, the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament's experts), with deaths valued like every death and the future lost counted through the discount rate. It is more than ten times its peers because most of them work only on AI, and Rethink's typical nuclear project averts far more deaths per dollar than a typical AI project; it is above the Nuclear Threat Initiative and Ploughshares Fund because nearly all of its work is on nuclear risk at a typical project's value, with no grants whose other funders might have paid. The biggest uncertainty is how much a dollar of such work cuts the risk (Rethink calls its figures placeholders; the range runs ten times either way); the result also moves with the years a cut counts and the discount rate. The one branch is discounted for missing data: no outcome of the work on the risk is measured.

How far the typical project's effect applies to this charity's work
rows.explainer: How far Rethink Priorities' typical small nuclear project applies to the Association's work: policy research, a journal of record (Arms Control Today), media work (its staff quoted by Reuters and the New York Times on Iran), congressional engagement and coalition building (the December 2024 strategy retreat of more than 50 campaigners from 28 organisations). Above typical for its standing: 54 years in the field, its briefs and fact sheets used by Congress and journalists. Below for public education and membership, whose path to the risk is longest. 0.8 (0.35 to 1.2), our judgment, the figure Ploughshares' model gives its grants to the same kind of work, the Association named among them (gr_evidence_adj), and NTI's for its mix of policy work and public education.

rows.label: Share of the work no one else would have done now
rows.explainer: Whether the research, journalism and advocacy would have been done now by other groups: the Center for Arms Control and Non-Proliferation, the Federation of American Scientists, the Stimson Center and the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists overlap, but the field is small and few cover arms control in such depth for Congress and the press. 0.7 (0.4 to 0.9), our judgment, the figure Ploughshares' model gives the same question for its grantees (gr_cf_other_orgs) and NTI's counterfactual_adj; that the work would have come years later is in years_of_impact.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: The Association's share of the resources behind its work, with what partners give unpaid: outside experts write much of Arms Control Today; the Physicists Coalition's scientists give their time (27 of them met 52 congressional offices in its 2025 DC Engagement Days, Ploughshares annual report, grantee spotlight); partners' staff come to its retreat and briefings. Worked: about $0.2M of such time a year (journal authors, the scientists' days, partners at events, our rough count) beside $1.69M of cost, about 0.9 (0.75 to 1), our judgment. Ploughshares' grants ($178,000 to the Association in the same year, Schedule I) are in the cost, so they lower nothing here; Ploughshares' model credits its grant as the same share of this work (gr_attribution_share_shared 0.95 over all 46 grantees), and its own coalitions, where the Association's staff take part, are discounted there for partners' time (own_attribution_share_shared), so no dollar's effect is counted twice.

rows.label: Benefits not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Good beyond the catastrophes counted, each part a share of the modelled value: work against a single detonation or a limited nuclear war (the test moratorium, Iran's and North Korea's programmes), which kills far fewer than 10% of people and has no shared forecast (nuclear_smaller_per_year 0), 8%; the conventional and chemical arms control in other_cost_share (7% of the cost, its harms far smaller than a nuclear war's), 1%; the journal and fact sheets as a public record other groups and teachers use, 1%. 10% (0 to 30%) in all, our judgment, as NTI's 10% and Ploughshares' 8% for the first kind.

rows.label: Harm: speeding up dangerous capabilities, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: A typical project's chance of backfiring is already in the shared cut per dollar (Rethink Priorities' backfire step). Research, journalism and advocacy on arms control can't speed up any capability. 0, down to −5%, our judgment.

rows.label: Harm: information hazards and attention, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire (in the shared cut): advocacy for restraint could, some argue, weaken deterrence or provoke a backlash, and alarming public messages can feed fatalism; none is shown to happen, and the Association publishes no technical weapons detail. 0, down to −5%, our judgment, as Ploughshares.
